label: Store ID
definition: The short code for your store, like MAIN_STORE. Everyone at the store types it to sign in, on the website and the app.
where: Sign in, top bar, welcome email

label: Store
definition: One shop or restaurant using RetailOps. Each store has its own data, its own logins and its own settings, kept apart from every other store.

label: Owner
definition: The person who asked for the store's account. Their login is the store's first admin, so they can add everyone else.

label: Staff
definition: Anyone at the store who isn't an admin. Staff see only the pages an admin ticked for them on Users.

label: KloudC master
definition: A KloudC team login that reviews new stores and looks after the platform. Masters sign in with Store ID PLATFORM and a two-step code. They don't use a store's pages.

label: Two-step sign-in
definition: A second check at sign-in: after your password you type a 6-digit code from an authenticator app on your phone. The code changes every 30 seconds.

label: Request access
definition: How a new store asks for a RetailOps account. A person at KloudC reviews every request before the store is set up.

label: Demo store
definition: A made-up store with sample data (Store ID DEMO), reset every night. You can look around everything, but nothing can be changed and nothing is ever sent.
where: Sign in with Store ID DEMO

label: Store time zone
definition: The time zone your store runs on. Every date, deadline, alert and "today" in RetailOps uses it, wherever you are.

label: Store week
definition: Monday to Sunday in the store's time zone. Skip this week lasts until Monday at midnight.

label: Appearance (light and dark)
definition: Whether RetailOps shows light or dark colours, or follows your device. Each person chooses for themselves.
where: Website user menu, app More › Account

label: Face ID
definition: Sign in to the app with your face or fingerprint instead of typing your password. It only works on the phone where you turned it on.

label: POS (point of sale)
definition: The till system your store rings sales on: for you, {pos}. RetailOps reads sales, menus and stock from it. It never changes anything in your POS.

label: Sales sync
definition: The nightly copy of yesterday's orders from {pos} into RetailOps. Past days are then checked against {pos} during the day and fixed if they changed.

label: Inventory upload
definition: The daily stock file from {pos} that you upload, with each item's count, price, cost and vendor. Reports always use the most recent one.

label: Retail items export
definition: The file {pos} gives you with every retail item and its stock (CSV or Excel). Upload it exactly as it comes: columns are matched by their header names.

label: On hand
definition: How many of an item the store has right now, from the latest inventory upload (or {pos}'s live count when Inventory from {pos} is on). It includes the Container.
where: Reorder, New order, cart, Fix Issues

label: Container
definition: A second storage place, like a back room or shipping container. In {pos} it is a second row for the same item with no price. RetailOps adds it to the shelf count.
where: New order, Fix Issues, Inventory Reports

label: Item
definition: One product your store sells, as it is set up in {pos}: a name, a price, a barcode and the vendors it comes from.

label: Vendor code (SKU)
definition: The vendor's own code for an item. It prints on the PO so the vendor knows exactly what you mean. Every product search also finds items by vendor code.

label: Barcode (UPC/EAN)
definition: The scannable number on the package. A valid one has the right length and check digit. Fix Issues lists items with a missing or invalid barcode.

label: Business day
definition: {pos}'s day for its own reports, which ends at 4 AM instead of midnight. Insights count by it. Items Sold counts by when each item was paid for.

label: Receiving number
definition: The number {pos} gives a delivery when it is received there (like IN378). It comes with the next inventory upload and helps find deliveries.

label: Kitchen item
definition: Food made in the store from the kitchen or catering menus. Kitchen items are left out of stock checks because they have no barcode or shelf count.
where: Fix Issues, Prep forecast, Menu trends

label: Vendor
definition: A supplier you buy from. Items are linked to vendors in {pos}, and each vendor gets its own cart, PO and schedule.

label: Vendor contact
definition: An email address saved for a vendor on Vendor contacts. Send PO can only email addresses saved here.

label: Vendor minimum order
definition: Most vendors only deliver when an order is big enough. That is why an Order due chip turns red only when 5 or more items need ordering.

label: Delivery days
definition: The weekdays a vendor delivers to your store. Set once per vendor on the Vendor Calendar.

label: Order deadline
definition: The last day to place an order so it comes on the next delivery day. It is set as a number of days before delivery.

label: Vendor schedule
definition: A vendor's delivery days plus its order deadline. With a schedule, lead times, Orders due and reminders work out by themselves.

label: Lookback
definition: How many days of past sales are used to work out an average. Longer is steadier. Shorter reacts faster to change.

label: Weekly sales
definition: Units of an item sold per week on average, counting only days it was in stock. Select it to see the week by week numbers.

label: Days of stock
definition: How many days the stock on hand will last at the current rate of sales. Few days left on a steady seller makes it Critical.

label: Reorder candidate
definition: An item expected to run out before the next delivery you could still order for. Reorder Candidates lists them for every vendor at once.

label: Supplier Projection (New order)
definition: The page that builds one vendor's order: how much of each item you need for the period you pick, with a suggested quantity.

label: Purchase order (PO)
definition: The order document for one vendor: your store's letterhead, then each item's vendor code, name and quantity, grouped by PO section. It is a PDF.

label: Purchase Order Cart
definition: One shared cart per vendor where the next order is built. Everyone with cart access sees the same lines, on the website and the app.

label: Case of (pack size)
definition: How many units are in one case. In the cart, Qty is cases and Case of is units per case, so Qty 2 with Case of 12 is 24 units.

label: CC
definition: Extra email addresses that get a copy of a PO sent with Send PO. A vendor contact can have up to 10 default CC addresses.

label: Placed order
definition: An order that really went to the vendor: marked Order placed, or emailed with Send PO. Only placed orders count as ordered.

label: Delivery
definition: Stock arriving from a vendor. Confirming a delivery in Delivery Review logs it as a purchase.

label: Unassigned
definition: Items with no vendor in {pos}. They can't go into a vendor's cart from Reorder. Add them by hand on the cart under the right vendor.

label: Delivery Review
definition: The page where deliveries found in your uploads are checked and confirmed. Confirming writes the purchase log.

label: Net change
definition: How much an item's count went up between two uploads, plus what sold in between. 100 on hand, 400 delivered and 50 sold shows 400.

label: Purchase log
definition: The record of what the store bought: item, vendor, quantity, date and cost. Delivery Review and Log a purchase write it. Reconciliation reads it.

label: Invoice
definition: A vendor's bill for a delivery. Upload it on Invoices: it is saved, shared on WhatsApp and emailed to {pos} as a PDF.

label: Reconciliation
definition: Comparing what you bought, sold and counted for each item to spot missing stock. Expected closing = opening count + purchased - sold.

label: Issue list
definition: One of the lists on Fix Issues, such as Missing barcodes or Negative inventory. Each tile shows how many are still open.

label: Close reason
definition: Why you closed an item on Fix Issues. Fixed reasons are checked again on the next upload. Not an issue stays closed for good.

label: Snooze
definition: Hide something for a while. It comes back by itself: a new item given more time on Fix Issues, or a Critical vendor set to Remind me later.

label: Category lead
definition: The person who looks after one PO section's items on Fix Issues. They get one Team task a day with their open items.

label: Vendor lead
definition: The person who looks after one vendor's items on Fix Issues when the item's PO section has no lead.

label: Shelf row
definition: The priced row for an item in {pos}, the stock out on the shop floor. Its pair with no price is the Container row.

label: Ask Inventory Bot
definition: A chat helper that answers questions in plain words by reading the same reports you see. It can't change anything.

label: Label Scanner
definition: The store's label app for scanning items and printing price labels. On the website it opens from the menu when the store has one.

label: Print label
definition: Send an item's price label to the store's label printer from the Scan tab. Print label history lets you reprint.

label: Insights
definition: Reports built from {pos}'s analytics that {pos}'s own screens don't give you, like Daily compare and Prep forecast. Admins grant them.

label: Also in {pos}
definition: Insights that repeat {pos}'s own reports (Sales channels, Check size & guests, Busy hours, Best & worst sellers), kept here so you don't have to switch.

label: Check
definition: One bill in {pos}. An order can be split into several checks.

label: Open check
definition: A check {pos} hasn't closed yet. Some are fine (paid orders waiting for pickup). Others were simply forgotten.

label: Menu trends
definition: Which items sold more or less than in the days just before, and which menu items didn't sell at all.

label: Team
definition: A group of people at the store, such as Kitchen or Front. Teams get their own chat, and a task sent to a team can be done by anyone in it.

label: Task
definition: Something one person or team needs to do, with an optional due time, steps, photo or note. Finish it with a swipe or a tap.

label: Recurring task
definition: A task template that creates itself on a schedule (daily, weekdays, weekly or monthly), with the same steps each time.

label: Task stats
definition: Admins only: per person, how many tasks were done, on time or late, and the usual time from created to done.

label: Team chat
definition: The chat for one team. Everyone in the team can read and post in it.

label: Direct message
definition: A private chat between two people. Either person can pin messages, hide the conversation or block the other.

label: Pinned message
definition: A chat message kept at the top of the chat. Up to 20 per chat.

label: @mention
definition: Type @ and a name in chat. That person is told even if they muted the chat.

label: Voice note
definition: A recorded message in chat, up to 5 minutes. Everyone can play them. Recording works in the app and in browsers that support it.

label: Seen by
definition: On your own chat message, who has read it and who hasn't yet.

label: News
definition: Announcements from managers to teams. Some ask you to confirm you read them.

label: Reported message
definition: A message, task or comment someone flagged as breaking the Team rules. Admins review every report within 24 hours.

label: Team rules
definition: What everyone agrees to before using Tasks, Chat and News: no abusive or objectionable content, and reports are acted on.

label: Daily checklist
definition: A list of questions staff answer each day, such as the closing checks. Submitting saves it under your login and shares a summary on WhatsApp.

label: Checklist builder
definition: Where admins build and change checklists, like a form builder: questions, sections, photos, versions and public links.

label: Public checklist link
definition: A web link that lets someone without an account fill in one checklist and nothing else. Turning it off stops the old link at once.

label: WhatsApp group
definition: A WhatsApp group the store's WhatsApp number is in. Checklists, invoices and flyers post to the groups an admin chooses.

label: Today card
definition: The card at the top of Home with what needs doing today: orders due, critical vendors and the closing checklist.

label: Critical vendor
definition: A vendor with steady sellers that are out of stock or about to be. It shows on Home until it is dealt with.

label: Weekly digest
definition: A short written summary of the last 7 days, made when you ask for it. The numbers come from the reports; the AI only writes the sentences.

label: Quiet hours
definition: No phone alerts are sent between 10 PM and 7 AM store time. Alerts due then wait until morning.

label: Phone alert
definition: A notification on your phone from the RetailOps app, such as Order due or Task assigned. Choose yours in the app under More › Notifications.

label: Integration
definition: A connection to another service: your POS, WhatsApp, email or the AI key. An admin sets each one up on Integrations and tests it.

label: Brand colour
definition: Your store's own colour, used on buttons and the menu. A master sets it with your logo. Text always stays easy to read.

label: Starter pack
definition: The ready-made set a new store starts with: checklists, PO sections, leads, flyer types and menu groups. A master picks it when approving a request.

label: Provisioning
definition: Setting up a newly approved store by itself: its database, starter pack and owner login. It takes a minute or two.

label: Suspend
definition: Pause a store: nobody can sign in and the app shows a maintenance message. Its data stays. Resume undoes it.

label: Resume
definition: Turn a suspended store back on. People can sign in again straight away.

label: Archive
definition: Off-board a store: sign-in is refused and the store is hidden. Its data is kept until it is purged. You type the Store ID to confirm.

label: Shared hosting
definition: The normal set-up: a store runs on KloudC's shared servers with its own separate database.

label: Dedicated server
definition: A store's own server, for stores that need it. A move needs a master's approval and can be rolled back within 7 days.

label: Audit log
definition: The record of every sign-in and every change on the platform: who, what, which store and when. Entries can't be changed.

label: Support session
definition: A short, time-limited sign-in to a store by a KloudC master to help with a problem. The reason is written to the audit log.

label: Object storage
definition: A storage service for files, such as Cloudflare R2 or Amazon S3. Each store's files sit in their own folder in one bucket.

label: Background job
definition: Work the server does away from the screen, such as a nightly sales sync or a data export. A failed job is tried again a few times.

label: Worker
definition: A server process that takes background jobs from the queue and runs them. Several workers can share one queue safely.

label: Live updates
definition: How a change saved on one server process reaches the others, so open lists refresh by themselves.

label: Usage
definition: How much of RetailOps a store uses: users, items, files, records, sales brought in, checks with the POS and AI questions. Sizes and counts are measured each night; until the first measurement they read "Not measured yet".
where: Setup › Data & usage; console › Usage & plan

label: Plan
definition: The package a store is on: Custom, Trial, Starter or Pro. Each plan has its own limits; Custom has none.
where: Setup › Data & usage; console › Usage & plan

label: Limit
definition: The most users, items or file storage a plan includes. Near the limit means 80% or more; over the limit is flagged, but work is never blocked.

label: Data export
definition: One ZIP file with everything a store keeps: a spreadsheet (CSV) per table, every stored file, and a checksum list. Passwords, sign-in tokens and saved keys are never in it.
where: Setup › Data & usage › Export all data

label: Download link
definition: A private link to a data export that stops working after a few hours. Making a new link ends the old one.

label: Off-boarding
definition: Closing a store's account: Archived, a final data export, Deleting on a date after the grace period, then Deleted.

label: Grace period
definition: The days between archiving a store and deleting its data. Deletion can be cancelled any time before the date.

label: Delete store data
definition: The last off-boarding step: the store's database, files and saved keys are deleted for good. Only the store's name and history in the audit log stay.

label: Item vendor
definition: A supplier you buy an item from. An item can have several, in order: the first is the first choice when ordering.
where: Item vendors, Reorder, New order, purchase orders

label: Vendor item code
definition: The vendor's own number for an item, printed on purchase orders so the vendor can find it fast. Optional.

label: Connect with Clover
definition: Signing in to Clover and approving RetailOps, so it can read your sales, items and stock. You can disconnect at any time.

label: Merchant ID
definition: Clover's ID for your store, 13 letters and digits. Find it in your Clover dashboard under Account & Setup.

label: API token
definition: A long secret key a POS gives you so another program can read your data. RetailOps saves it encrypted and only ever shows its last 4 characters.

label: Temporary password
definition: A password made for a new master, shown once. They sign in with it and must choose their own before using the console.

label: Platform setting
definition: A setting for the whole platform, not one store, changed in the console. A value saved there wins over the server's own value until you reset it.

label: New store sign-ups
definition: Whether the public sign-up page takes requests from new stores. Off: it says sign-ups are closed. Existing stores are not affected.

label: Store health
definition: A store's status at a glance in the console: database version, the last run of each background job, last activity and its connections.

label: Store time
definition: Dates and "today" always follow your store's time zone, wherever you are. After midnight in your store it's the next day here too.
where: Every date on the website and app
